verses.zh: 以笏死后，以色列人又行耶和华眼中看为恶的事，
verses.en: The Israelites again did evil in the Lord’s sight[NOTE:1] after Ehud’s death.
notes: Heb “did evil in the eyes of the Lord.”
verses.commentary:
4:1 "the sons of Israel again did evil in the sight of the Lord" This is a recurrent phrase
throughout the period of the Judges. The evil spoken of here is that they worshiped the fertility gods of Canaan.

-
SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANCIENT NEAR EAST

verses.zh: 耶和华就把他们付与在夏琐作王的迦南王耶宾手中；他的将军是西西拉，住在外邦人的夏罗设。
verses.en: The Lord turned them over to[NOTE:1] King Jabin of Canaan, who ruled in Hazor.[NOTE:2] The general of his army was Sisera, who lived in Harosheth Haggoyim.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “the Lord sold them into the hands of.”
For location see Map1-D2; Map2-D3; Map3-A2; Map4-C1.tn Or “King Jabin of Hazor, a Canaanite ruler.”
Or “Harosheth of the Pagan Nations”; cf. KJV “Harosheth of the Gentiles.” “Haroshet” may mean “Forest [area]” or be a reference to some sort of carving.
verses.commentary:
4:2 "the Lord sold them into the hand of" Again, this is the opposite of the term
"redeemed" (see note at Jdgs. 2:14 and 3:8).

▣ "Jabin king of Canaan" There is another Jabin (BDB 108) mentioned in Joshua 11 who was killed by
Joshua and was also the king of Hazor. Many have tried to say that these two accounts are a jumbled account of that one
event. However, the term "Jabin" may be a family name or a title for the kings of Hazor, as "pharaoh" is for Egypt, "Hadad"
is for Syria, and later "Caesar" is for Rome.

The title "king of Canaan" is unique and unusual.

- NET Bible changes it to "King Jabin of Canaan"; TEV has "Jabin, a Canaanite King"

- he may have led a confederacy of Canaanite city-states (note Jos. 11:10)

- it may have been an honorific title for the leader of the largest, most powerful Canaanite city of its day

Surprisingly, he is not mentioned in the poetic account of Judges 5.

▣ "who reigned in Hazor" Hazor is a site about eight and a half miles north of the Sea of Galilee. It is a
huge archaeological site. Megiddo, another city in the north, is about 40 acres, but Hazor is 240 acres. This was the chief
Canaanite stronghold of the north. It was destroyed by Joshua in Joshua 11. There were not enough Israelis to occupy all
the cities and possibly it was reoccupied by Canaanites.

▣ "and the commander of his army was Sisera" Sisera (BDB 696) is not a Hebrew or Canaanite name and
we do not know his origin (may be Philistine, AB, p. 94), but he was the military commander for the Canaanite city-state of Hazor.

▣ "who lived in Harosheth-hagoyim" The location is uncertain but the name means "forest of the nations"
or "international forest" (BDB 361 II).

verses.zh: 耶宾王有铁车九百辆。他大大欺压以色列人二十年，以色列人就呼求耶和华。
verses.en: The Israelites cried out for help to the Lord because Sisera[NOTE:1] had 900 chariots with iron-rimmed wheels,[NOTE:2] and he cruelly[NOTE:3] oppressed the Israelites for 20 years.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Sisera) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

Regarding the translation “chariots with iron-rimmed wheels,” see Y. Yadin, The Art of Warfare in Biblical Lands, 255, and the article by R. Drews, “The ‘Chariots of Iron’ of Joshua and Judges,” JSOT 45 (1989): 15-23.
Heb “with strength.”
verses.commentary:
4:3 "for he had 900 iron chariots" Iron is something that the Hebrews did not possess early at this period of their
history. At the time, only the Philistines had iron weapons (cf. 1 Sam. 13:19-21). This does not mean the entire chariots were
iron but just

- their ornaments (i.e., breast plates for horses and chariots; the chariots allowed the indigenous Canaanites to control the
valleys but not the foothills

- their wheels

Nine hundred chariots is far too many for one Canaanite city, so this must mean that a coalition of Canaanite
city-states joined together to repel the invading Israelites.

verses.zh: 有一位女先知名叫底波拉，是拉比多的妻，当时作以色列的士师。
verses.en: Now Deborah, a prophetess,[NOTE:1] wife of Lappidoth, was[NOTE:2] leading[NOTE:3] Israel at that time.
notes: Heb “ a woman, a prophetess.” In Hebrew idiom the generic “woman” sometimes precedes the more specific designation. See GKC 437-38 §135.b.
Heb “she was.” The pronoun refers back to the nominative absolute “Deborah.” Hebrew style sometimes employs such resumptive pronouns when lengthy qualifiers separate the subject from the verb.
Or “judging.”
verses.commentary:
4:4 "Now Deborah, a prophetess" Deborah means "bee" (BDB 184). There are many women in places of leadership
in the OT. Miriam in Exod. 15:20; Huldah in 2 Kgs. 24:14, were called prophetesses. Noadiah in Neh. 6:14 was a false prophetess.
Anna in Luke 2:36; Phoebe in Rom. 16:1; Philip's daughters in Acts 21:9; and the widow's list of 1 Tim. 3:11 also had positions
of leadership in the NT. It is true that the norm (i.e., patriarchal culture) is God using a man to lead His people, but the fact that
we have these notable exceptions shows that any dogmatic statement about women's leadership is inappropriate! One must
balance Paul's strong statements in this matter to the culture of his day. The issue is far from easy to solve but must be thought
through clearly, biblically, not emotionally, culturally, or denominationally!

- SPECIAL TOPIC: WOMEN IN THE BIBLE

- SPECIAL TOPIC: WOMEN IN MINISTRY

- SPECIAL TOPIC: WOMEN KEEP
SILENT

▣ "the wife of Lappidoth" His name means "torches" (BDB 542). Many have believed that because Barak,
Deborah's general's name means "lightening" (BDB 140), that maybe she was married to her general, but this seems to be
reading too much into the similarities of these two names. Some commentators have asserted that this man's name is a
FEMININE form but in truth it is not FEMININE but an ABSTRACT CONSTRUCT.

verses.zh: 她住在以法莲山地拉玛和伯特利中间，在底波拉的棕树下。以色列人都上她那里去听判断。
verses.en: She would sit[NOTE:1] under the Date Palm Tree of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel[NOTE:2] in the Ephraimite hill country. The Israelites would come up to her to have their disputes settled.[NOTE:3]
notes: That is, “consider legal disputes.”
For location see Map4-G4; Map5-C1; Map6-E3; Map7-D1; Map8-G3.
Heb “for judgment.”
verses.commentary:
4:5 "the palm tree" Trees often had special cultic association, as the oaks of Moreh (cf. Gen. 12:6) in the life of
Abraham. See also Jdgs. 6:11, 19; 9:6, 37; 1 Sam. 10:3; 18:9, 10; 1 Kgs. 13:14; 1 Chr. 10:12.

▣ "the sons of Israel came up to her for judgment" This shows that she was more than just a local judge
for she seems to have judged in the south and delivered the north.

verses.zh: 她打发人从拿弗他利的基低斯将亚比挪庵的儿子巴拉召了来，对他说：「耶和华―以色列的　神吩咐你说：『你率领一万拿弗他利和西布伦人上他泊山去。
verses.en: She summoned[NOTE:1] Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali. She said to him, “Is it not true that the Lord God of Israel is commanding you? Go, march to Mount Tabor! Take with you 10,000 men from Naphtali and Zebulun.
notes: Heb “sent and summoned.”
verses.commentary:
4:6 "Barak the son of Abinoam from Kadesh-naphtali" Barak (BDB 140) means "lightening." This location must be
differentiated from Kadesh-barnea in the south. Barak was from the area affected by the control of the Canaannite city of Hazor.

In a sense Deborah is not a typical "judge." She actually, and uniquely in Judges, functions as a person
who settles legal and religious disputes (cf. Jdgs. 4:5). It is Barak who is the typical military leader/judge, common in Judges.
He is listed with other judges in Hebrew 11:32, but Deborah is not mentioned. Deborah is a prophetess, not a judge in the
military sense.

▣ "Mount Tabor" Mount Tabor is an isolated hill northeast of the plains of Megiddo or the Valley of Esdraelon
(cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 4, p. 1246). Because it was a hill, the chariots of Sisera were not effective against it.

▣ "ten thousand" The OT uses (1) hyperbolic numbers or (2) idioms to express groups (cf. Jdgs. 4:10,14).
Modern westerners misunderstand this imagery (see D. Brent Sandy, Plowshares and Pruning Hooks: Rethinking the
Language of Biblical Prophecy and Apocalyptic.

- SPECIAL TOPIC: THOUSAND (eleph)

- SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS
IN SCRIPTURE

▣ "the sons of Naphtali and from the sons of Zebulun" These are two of the tribes in the tribal allocation
affected by the Canaanite city of Hazor. In Judges 5 we learn that many more of the tribes were involved, probably the two
primary groups came from these two northern tribes.

verses.zh: 我必使耶宾的将军西西拉率领他的车辆和全军往基顺河，到你那里去；我必将他交在你手中。』」
verses.en: I will bring Sisera, the general of Jabin’s army, to you at the Kishon River, along with his chariots and huge army.[NOTE:1] I will hand him over to you.”
notes: Heb “horde”; “multitude.”
verses.commentary:
4:7

NASB, NKJV, TEV
"river"

NRSV, JPSOA, REB, LXX
"wadi"

NJB
"torrent"

This term (BDB 636) refers to a ravine where water rushes through during the months of snow melt and
rain storms (Jdgs. 5:21; Ps. 83:10), but is dry the rest of the year. These dry wadis were often used as roads.

verses.zh: 巴拉说：「你若同我去，我就去；你若不同我去，我就不去。」
verses.en: Barak said to her, “If you go with me, I will go. But if you do not go with me, I will not go.”

verses.zh: 底波拉说：「我必与你同去，只是你在所行的路上得不着荣耀，因为耶和华要将西西拉交在一个妇人手里。」于是底波拉起来，与巴拉一同往基低斯去了。
verses.en: She said, “I will indeed go with you. But you will not gain fame[NOTE:1] on the expedition you are undertaking,[NOTE:2] for the Lord will turn Sisera over to a woman.”[NOTE:3] Deborah got up and went with Barak to Kedesh.
notes: Or “honor.”

Heb “on [account of (?)] the way which you are walking.” Another option is to translate, “due to the way you are going about this.” In this case direct reference is made to Barak’s hesitancy as the reason for his loss of glory.
Heb “for into the hands of a woman the Lord will sell Sisera.”
verses.commentary:
4:9 "She said, I will surely go with you" This is an intensified grammar feature (an INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE
and an IMPERFECT VERB from the same root, BDB 229, KB 246).

Barak wanted Deborah close by in case he needed to consult YHWH.

▣ "the honor shall not be yours" This has two possible references.

- Deborah accompanying Barak

- Jael, the wife of Heber, the Kenite, killing the army commander Sisera, Jdgs. 4:17-22

verses.zh: 巴拉就招聚西布伦人和拿弗他利人到基低斯，跟他上去的有一万人。底波拉也同他上去。
verses.en: Barak summoned men from Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh, and 10,000 men followed him;[NOTE:1] Deborah went up with him as well.
notes: Heb “went up at his feet.”

verses.zh: 摩西岳父（或译：内兄）何巴的后裔，基尼人希百曾离开基尼族，到靠近基低斯、撒拿音的橡树旁支搭帐棚。
verses.en: Now Heber the Kenite had moved away[NOTE:1] from the Kenites, the descendants of Hobab, Moses’ father-in-law. He lived[NOTE:2] near the great tree in Zaanannim near Kedesh.
notes: Or “separated.”
Heb “pitched his tent.”
verses.commentary:
4:11 "Now Heber the Kenite" This short verse is inserted to explain the presence of Jael in Jdgs. 4:17 and her
significant role in the death of Sisera. The Kenites are a Midianite tribe (cf. Jdgs. 1:13,16; Num. 10:29). Moses' father-in-law
was a member of this people group, as was Caleb.

verses.zh: 有人告诉西西拉说：「亚比挪庵的儿子巴拉已经上他泊山了。」
verses.en: When Sisera heard[NOTE:1] that Barak son of Abinoam had gone up to Mount Tabor,
notes: Heb “and they told Sisera.”

verses.zh: 西西拉就聚集所有的铁车九百辆和跟随他的全军，从外邦人的夏罗设出来，到了基顺河。
verses.en: he[NOTE:1] ordered[NOTE:2] all his chariotry—900 chariots with iron-rimmed wheels—and all the troops he had with him to go from Harosheth Haggoyim to the Kishon River.
notes: Heb “Sisera.” The proper name has been replaced by the pronoun (“he”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Or “summoned.”

verses.zh: 底波拉对巴拉说：「你起来，今日就是耶和华将西西拉交在你手的日子。耶和华岂不在你前头行吗？」于是巴拉下了他泊山，跟随他有一万人。
verses.en: Deborah said to Barak, “Spring into action,[NOTE:1] for this is the day the Lord is handing Sisera over to you![NOTE:2] Has the Lord not taken the lead?”[NOTE:3] So Barak went down from Mount Tabor with 10,000 men following him.
notes: Heb “Arise!”

The verb form (a Hebrew perfect, indicating completed action from the standpoint of the speaker) emphasizes the certainty of the event. Though it had not yet taken place, the Lord speaks of it as a “done deal.”
Heb “Has the Lord not gone out before you?”
verses.commentary:
4:14 "the Lord has gone out before you" This is "holy war" terminology
(cf. Deut. 1:30; 3:22; 2 Sam. 5:24). Victory came only because of YHWH's presence not the power, skill, or numbers of the
Israeli army. Note Jdgs. 4:15, "the Lord routed Sisera" and Jdgs. 4:23, "So God subdued on
that day Jabin the king of Canaan."

YHWH uses human instrumentality.

- Moses ‒ Exod. 3:8-10

- here

- Deborah

- Barak (cf. Heb. 11:32)

- Jael

verses.zh: 耶和华使西西拉和他一切车辆全军溃乱，在巴拉面前被刀杀败；西西拉下车步行逃跑。
verses.en: The Lord routed[NOTE:1] Sisera, all his chariotry, and all his army with the edge of the sword.[NOTE:2] Sisera jumped out of[NOTE:3] his chariot and ran away on foot.
notes: Or “caused to panic.”
The Hebrew text also includes the phrase “before Barak.” This has not been included in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “got down from.”
verses.commentary:
4:15 "The Lord routed Sisera. . .alighted from his chariot" We learn from Jdgs. 5:4, 5,
and 21 that apparently the Lord had caused a huge thunderstorm to soften the ground so that the iron chariots bogged down
in the Valley of Esdeaelon. They had to abandon their chariots, which were their only means of superiority.

This VERB (BDB 243, KB 251, Qal IMPERFECT with waw)
means "to confuse" or "vex," and is used of YHWH confusing the Egyptian honor guard at the Red Sea with the Shekinah
cloud of glory separating the Israelites (cf. Exod. 14:24; also note Jos. 10:10).

verses.zh: 巴拉追赶车辆、军队，直到外邦人的夏罗设。西西拉的全军都倒在刀下，没有留下一人。
verses.en: Now Barak chased the chariots and the army all the way to Harosheth Haggoyim. Sisera’s whole army died[NOTE:1] by the edge of the sword; not even one survived![NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “fell.”
Heb “was left.”
verses.commentary:
4:16 "not even one was left" This is also "holy war" terminology (cf. Exod. 14:28; Ps. 83:9). This is what YHWH had
commanded of Israel.

verses.zh: 只有西西拉步行逃跑，到了基尼人希百之妻雅亿的帐棚，因为夏琐王耶宾与基尼人希百家和好。
verses.en: Now Sisera ran away on foot to the tent of Jael, wife of Heber the Kenite, for King Jabin of Hazor[NOTE:1] and the family of Heber the Kenite had made a peace treaty.[NOTE:2]
notes: For location see Map1-D2; Map2-D3; Map3-A2; Map4-C1.
Heb “for there was peace between.”
verses.commentary:
4:17 "Jael" Her name (BDB418) means "mountain-goat" (cf. Job 39:1; Ps. 104:18).

▣ "for there was peace between Jabin the king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite" Some scholars
have suggested that "the Kenites" (related to Cain) were metal workers (cf. Gen. 4:22) and that Heber helped build the iron
chariots and other weaponry for Hazor. This is just interesting speculation.

verses.zh: 雅亿出来迎接西西拉，对他说：「请我主进来，不要惧怕」；西西拉就进了她的帐棚。雅亿用被将他遮盖。
verses.en: Jael came out to welcome Sisera. She said to him, “Stop and rest,[NOTE:1] my lord. Stop and rest with me. Don’t be afraid.” So Sisera[NOTE:2] stopped to rest in her tent, and she put a blanket over him.
notes: Heb “Turn aside” (also a second time later in this verse).
Heb “he”; the referent (Sisera) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
verses.commentary:
4:18 "And he turned aside to her into the tent" Apparently from Bedouin examples, the women had separate tents
and Jael must have had a tent to herself (note Gen. 31:33). She tricked him into thinking he was safe under her cloak, but then
she drove a tent peg through his temple (cf. Jdgs. 4:21). Remember, the women were the ones who set up the tents and she
would have had these tools and the ability to use them.

▣ "with a rug" This word (BDB 970) occurs only here. It is similar to "mantle" (BDB 971), which refers to an
outer garment (cf. Gen. 35:2; Ruth 3:3). See NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 1255.

verses.zh: 西西拉对雅亿说：「我渴了，求你给我一点水喝。」雅亿就打开皮袋，给他奶子喝，仍旧把他遮盖。
verses.en: He said to her, “Give me a little water to drink because I’m thirsty.” She opened a goatskin container of milk and gave him some milk to drink. Then she covered him up again.

verses.zh: 西西拉又对雅亿说：「请你站在帐棚门口，若有人来问你说：『有人在这里没有？』你就说：『没有。』」
verses.en: He said to her, “Stand watch at the entrance to the tent. If anyone comes along and asks you, ‘Is there a man here?’ say, ‘No.’”

verses.zh: 西西拉疲乏沉睡。希百的妻雅亿取了帐棚的橛子，手里拿着锤子，轻悄悄地到他旁边，将橛子从他鬓边钉进去，钉入地里。西西拉就死了。
verses.en: Then Jael wife of Heber took a tent peg in one hand and a hammer in the other.[NOTE:1] She crept up on him, drove the tent peg through his temple into the ground[NOTE:2] while he was asleep from exhaustion,[NOTE:3] and he died.
notes: Heb “took a tent peg and put a hammer in her hand.”
Heb “and it went into the ground.”
Heb “and exhausted.” Another option is to understand this as a reference to the result of the fatal blow. In this case, the phrase could be translated, “and he breathed his last.”
verses.commentary:
4:21 "temple" Most English translations have "temple," but the word (BDB 956) occurs only in

- Jdgs. 4:21; 5:26

- Song of Songs 4:3; 6:7

Since it seems difficult to drive a stake through one's skull, it may refer to the upper neck behind the ear.

▣ "he was sound asleep" This PARTICIPLE (BDB 922, KB 1191, Niphal
ACTIVE PARTICIPLE) may denote something even stronger than "deep sleep," possibly "stunned." It is
even possible that Jael put something in the milk that drugged him (cf. Jdgs. 5:25; NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 1057).

verses.zh: 巴拉追赶西西拉的时候，雅亿出来迎接他说：「来吧，我将你所寻找的人给你看。」他就进入帐棚，看见西西拉已经死了，倒在地上，橛子还在他鬓中。
verses.en: Now Barak was chasing Sisera. Jael went out to welcome him. She said to him, “Come here and I will show you the man you are searching for.” He went with her into the tent,[NOTE:1] and there he saw Sisera sprawled out dead[NOTE:2] with the tent peg through his temple.
notes: Heb “he went to her.”
Heb “fallen, dead.”

verses.zh: 这样，　神使迦南王耶宾被以色列人制伏了。
verses.en: That day God humiliated King Jabin of Canaan before the Israelites.

verses.zh: 从此以色列人的手越发有力，胜了迦南王耶宾，直到将他灭绝了。
verses.en: Israel’s power continued to overwhelm[NOTE:1] King Jabin of Canaan until they did away with[NOTE:2] him.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “The hand of the Israelites became more and more severe against.”
Heb “cut off.”
Heb “Jabin king of Canaan.” The proper name and title have been replaced by the pronoun (“he”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.
verses.commentary:
4:24 These summary verses show that the Promised Land was taken in stages, not in one swift movement.

BRIEF INTRODUCTION

- Judges 3 primarily deals with problems in southern Canaan.

- Judges 4 primarily deals with problems in northern Canaan.

- Judges 4 is a prose account of Deborah's judging ministry, while Judges 5 is a poetic account of the same incident.
We learn from Egyptian documents that this was a quite common literary technique during this period and is one more
evidence of the historicity of the book of Judges.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 4:1-3

1Then the sons of Israel again did evil in the sight of the Lord, after Ehud died.
2And the Lord sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in
Hazor; and the commander of his army was Sisera, who lived in Harosheth-hagoyim. 3The sons of Israel cried
to theLord; for he had nine hundred iron chariots, and he oppressed the sons of Israel severely
for twenty years.
